**Finding submitted: `missing` (T4C — Termination for convenience), confidence 0.86**

**What I found**

- **Article IV (p0049)** sets a **36-month Initial Period**, renewable for a further **seven years at Licensor's sole option**, and contains no Licensee exit right.
- Searching the whole agreement, every termination trigger runs **in Licensor's favour**: breach (Art. II p0043 and Art. IV p0049), insolvency (Art. XIX p0132, mutual but not convenience), Change of Control (Art. XX p0134), and wind-up (p0137).
- **Article XXI (p0138)** and **Article XXIII (p0142)** reinforce that on any termination Licensor retains all rights, including payment entitlements — so exit is costly and one-sided.
- There is **no Licensor termination-for-convenience right**, so the walk-away trigger on that limb is not engaged; the gap is purely on our side.

**Why this is a deviation**

Under T4C, the absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (missing behaviour). Here the commitment is 36 months plus a unilateral seven-year renewal option, with volume-based fees, $2,500/month support and 33% Supplemental Payments continuing throughout.

**Redline proposed (validated `ok:true`)** — new Article IV.IV inserted after p0049:

> Termination for Convenience. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Licensee may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, without penalty, early termination charge, or acceleration of any user fees, Supplemental Payments or other amounts. Upon such termination, Licensor shall refund to Licensee any prepaid fees allocable to the period after the effective date of termination... Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any renewal or extension term.

The drafting deliberately blocks **acceleration of Supplemental Payments** on exit (the planner's flagged risk) and reaches the preferred position with a single insertion rather than restructuring Article IV. The negotiation comment offers the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a three-month fee cap) if Licensor pushes back.
